flows.title: Invoice status lifecycle
flows.summary: An invoice starts as Draft, is Issued to the customer, then ends as Paid or Void. Void is allowed from Draft or Issued but never from Paid. MarkPaid and Void are idempotent when repeated.
flows.plain_summary: An invoice moves through a few simple stages. It starts as a draft, is issued to the customer, and ends when it is either paid or cancelled. A draft or an issued invoice can be cancelled, but once an invoice is paid it can no longer be cancelled. Repeating a payment or a cancellation on an invoice that is already paid or cancelled changes nothing.

nodes.label: Draft
nodes.description: CreateDraft builds the invoice with Status = Draft; line items can be added while in this state.

nodes.label: Issued
nodes.description: Issue() requires Draft, stamps IssuedAtUtc and sets the due date (default +14 days).

nodes.label: Paid
nodes.description: MarkPaid() requires Issued and stamps PaidAtUtc. Calling it on a Paid invoice is a no-op.

nodes.label: Void
nodes.description: Void() is allowed from Draft or Issued, appends the reason to Notes, and is a no-op when already Void.

nodes.label: Paid cannot be voided
nodes.description: Voiding a Paid invoice throws InvalidOperationException.
nodes.snippet: throw new InvalidOperationException("Paid invoices cannot be voided.");

notes: The status transitions live in the Invoice aggregate. The HTTP endpoints (issue, pay, void) only call these methods, which I did not trace here.
MarkPaid on Draft throws; only Issued can be paid.
